terms.register: in poetry (Verg., Ov.) and post-Augustan prose (Plin.)
terms.comment: The adjective of medicus, the doctor. Cicero’s prose says it with the noun: the medical art is medicīna (see medicine), a doctor’s advice medicī cōnsilium, medical care cūrātiō (see treatment); a medical student is medicīnae studiōsus.
Not before Augustus (Lewis & Short); in Pliny of instruments and remedies.

phrases.latin: alitur vitium vīvitque tegendō, dum medicās adhibēre manūs ad volnera pāstor abnegat
phrases.english: the sore feeds and thrives by being covered up, while the shepherd refuses to put healing hands to the wounds
